challenges.says: The Disabled criterion for businessrule-56832565542674334637 drops its conditions: a list loses all values under its key even when the definition says to keep other entries, and the values left in place are those of a chosen item, a checkbox's on list and the policy's own on list, not only 'extra on values'.

The criteria use words a product owner who never saw the code cannot follow: 'presentation's default', 'spin box', 'expandable string', 'multiple-string value', '32-bit number', 'registry value' and 'extra values'.

The criteria for 'Unknown' state and 'registry value' (and the policy's 'on value', 'off value') are unexplained jargon, and 'only supplied settings are written' sits beside 'every option is written whatever its value' with nothing saying when each applies, so the two read as contradictory.

The last criterion cites decision-2 and scope.decision-13 for 'the write goes to the stored policy settings for the section', but decision-2 only says the registry source is modelled in Domain and filled from imported files, so neither decision carries that statement.

The criterion that state and comment 'come from the stored settings, not from the registry' cites decisions that do not say where a section's state is read from, so the fact is not carried by what it cites.

The Reset criterion cites layer-web although businessrule-27078270365699057081 owns the Reset behaviour (confirmation text and the restored header with blank lines), and the rule is cited only for Open File.

The 'Include SPOL header' criterion cites scope.decision-13, which only says SPOL text in and out is carried; the heading-and-blank-line fact comes from the shared-story rule the surface relies on, which a decision cannot carry.

The Apply story holds the option-saving rules while the state-writing rules (forget first, Enabled, Disabled) sit in the OK story, though both buttons run the same save; the split leaves Apply's own story depending on an unstated later story.

The criterion for businessrule-70167687024707690035 says 'the view refreshes either way' and gives both messages, but the rule's 'all policies to both sources and comments' and the failure-count wording 'N out of M' do not state when the first message shows versus the second, leaving the success condition ambiguous.
